extra.message: OS command injection. parseFile() builds a shell command by string concatenation ('let cmd = this.phpPath + " " + realFileName + " " + arg1 + " " + arg2') and passes it to child_process.exec(), which runs it through /bin/sh. arg1/arg2 are the user-controlled 'item' and 'price' query parameters extracted from the URL in routes/php.js (getJsonFromUrl -> execPHP.parseFile(queryParams.path, ..., queryParams.item, queryParams.price)). A request like GET /order.php?item=;cat%20/etc/passwd&price=1 makes the shell execute 'cat /etc/passwd', giving remote command execution.

extra.message: Path traversal. realFileName is built as this.phpFolder + fileName with no sanitization or containment check. fileName is queryParams.path, taken directly from the request URL path by routes/php.js ('*.php' route -> getJsonFromUrl(request.originalUrl) -> execPHP.parseFile(queryParams.path, ...)). A request such as GET /../some/dir/evil.php?item=a&price=b (sent with a raw, non-normalized path) resolves to './phpFiles/../some/dir/evil.php' and executes an arbitrary PHP file outside the phpFiles directory, allowing execution of any .php file readable on the server filesystem.

extra.message: Mass assignment in PUT /users/modify. The entire request body is used as the MongoDB update: 'var query = req.body;' then collection.findOneAndUpdate({ 'username': req.session.user.username }, { $set: query }). There is no field whitelist, so an attacker can $set arbitrary fields, including 'username'. Because the session is refreshed from the update result (lines 115-117, 'req.session.user = result'), an attacker can first change their own username to a victim's username and then issue a second update that matches and modifies the victim's document (e.g. changing the victim's password), resulting in full account takeover.

extra.message: Hardcoded session signing secret. The express-session middleware is initialized with secret: "Shh, its a secret!" committed in source code. extra.message: Insecure session configuration. The session cookie is created without the 'secure' flag (no 'secure: true' option, and the server only serves plain HTTP per bin/www), so session identifiers are transmitted unencrypted and can be intercepted. Additionally 'saveUninitialized: true' and 'resave: true' cause a session (and Set-Cookie) to be created and persisted for every anonymous request, wasting store resources and enabling trivially predictable session-creation behavior, with a 30-day expiry that greatly extends the window for cookie theft/replay.

extra.message: Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext. collection.insert(req.body) persists the raw 'password' field with no hashing or salting, authentication compares it verbatim (line 58: findOne({ username: ..., password: req.body.password })), and the client even defaults each user's password to their username (public/javascripts/global.js line 85). extra.message: Security misconfiguration: no security headers are set anywhere in the middleware stack (no X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, or Strict-Transport-Security, and no helmet package in package.json). As a result authenticated pages such as the login/admin interfaces can be embedded in attacker-controlled iframes and clickjacked, and pages are served without any browser hardening protections.

extra.message: Missing CSRF protection on all state-changing endpoints. POST /users/session (login), POST /users/adduser, PUT /users/modify and DELETE /users/deleteuser accept requests without any CSRF token, Origin/Referer validation, or SameSite cookie attribute, and the urlencoded bodies are parsed from cross-site form submissions. A malicious third-party page can silently log a victim into an attacker-controlled account (login CSRF), create accounts, or alter the logged-in victim's profile data via /users/modify.
